registration: not registered; zero-spend replay proposed for the aggregation-theory addendum

estimator.seed_rule: panel i of PANELS uses base 13 + 100 i (as effective_voter.json); topology cell j uses base 13 + 100 (4 + j); the fold split uses the base seed; all rules of a community share one resampling stream at base + 1; the reused effective_voter CV oracle keeps its own stream at the base seed
estimator.population: triples: all three r0 verdicts codable under code_response(extract_verdict(r0), 'published')
estimator.weighted_rule: log-odds weights log(p/(1-p)), p Laplace-smoothed seat accuracy on the other fold; sign of sum w_i (2 x_i - 1); exact tie -> simple majority
estimator.oracle: analyze_effective_voter.cv_oracle over the three r0 bits, fold fixed per item
estimator.t2_ceiling: gain <= p(1-p)(1-rho) for three voters of common competence p and mean pairwise error correlation rho (moment band over the eight profiles, LP-checked in --selftest)

weights.tie_rule: exact zero score falls back to the simple majority

t2_own_seats.note: seats are heterogeneous (lock): the common-p band is not the right object; the Shapley-Grofman rule is

t1.verdict: weighted rule EQUALS the neutral dictator on every debate
t1.note: the CV rule's lower tail comes from resamples in which the dominant seat's weight no longer exceeds the others' (share above); under lock the advocates' weights are gold base-rate logits, so an item resample that tilts the gold balance can make the two advocates jointly outweigh the neutral seat and the rule degenerates to a near-constant verdict; Shapley-Grofman optimality assumes conditional independence, which lock violates
